summary.headline: LMW Q1 FY27 revenue flat QoQ at ₹891 cr (+24% YoY); PBT ₹85 cr, with TMD order book at ₹3,200 cr and ATC order book near ₹1,000 cr.
summary.overview: Consolidated-level revenue was broadly flat sequentially at ₹891 cr against ₹889 cr in Q4 FY26 and up 24% YoY from ₹722 cr. PBT rose to ₹85 cr, up 18% QoQ and about 151% YoY from ₹34 cr. TMD revenue was ₹482 cr, roughly flat QoQ and up 16% YoY, while the TMD operating margin fell sequentially on lower turnover, which management attributed to volume and to rupee and commodity cost pressure. ATC revenue rose to ₹60 cr and margins improved, partly due to forex. LMW Global and LMW China losses narrowed QoQ, and China turnover fell sharply YoY.

segments.name: TMD (Textile Machinery Division)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹482 cr; order book ₹3,200 cr of which ~₹2,400 cr active; mix 64% domestic, 10% export, 26% spares. Capacity utilisation ~75-80%, though a later answer put textile utilisation at ~60%.

segments.name: Machine Tool Division (MTD) and Foundry
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹343 cr, with Foundry ~8% of the total. Automotive ~56% of MTD revenue. Management said MTD operating margin fell on lower turnover, and capacity can grow about 15-20% without major capex.

segments.name: ATC (Air Texturing/Composite-related)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹60 cr, ~90% export. Order book ~₹1,000 cr for execution over 3 to 3.5 years, with composite ~20% of turnover and ~25% of the order book. Margin improved, partly on forex and a higher assemblies mix.

segments.name: LMW Global (Dubai) and LMW China
segments.commentary: Global turnover ₹51 cr with ₹22 cr order book and ₹5.6 cr loss. China turnover ₹11 cr (vs ₹76 cr YoY) with ₹128 cr order book and ₹7 cr loss.

guidance_outlook: Management expects gradual, not sharp, recovery in spindle absorption. State policies (Gujarat, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh) and FTAs are cited as demand triggers.
Raw material and logistics costs are up about 3-3.5% per management, and supply-chain availability has eased but is still monitored for 4-5 months of pipeline cover.
ATC needs ~₹150 cr of new land and building capex, with a 18-24 month timeline.
MTD margin recovery depends on turnover growth and capacity utilisation; no timeline was given. Management also flagged price revisions and India-sourced substitutes for imported parts.
Auto-winder product: orders expected to be booked around the last quarter of this year.
capex_capacity: ATC: ~₹150 cr for new land and building under an MoU; 18-24 month build timeline.
MTD capacity utilisation ~75-80%; capacity can add ~15-20% without new capex, with further capex needed beyond that.
Textile machinery utilisation ~60% per a later answer.
Factory ownership: the land for the ATC facility is owned by the company, per management.
demand_pricing: TMD order book ₹3,200 cr (active ~₹2,400 cr). Order book is secured by a 10% customer deposit, and delivery lead times have shrunk from 14-15 months to much shorter.
Order mix is ~70% projects and ~30% unitary machines, against a typical 60:40 in good years.
Export orders for ATC ~₹900-1,000 cr over 3-3.5 years; ~₹150 cr of Global/China export orders are LC-backed and short cycle.
ATC order book is ~25% composite and ~75% metallics. Composite share is expected to build as exports rise.
MTD order book is short-cycle (under 3 months) and cash-backed, so it is not in the headline order book.
Management cited steep order inflow in the last quarter (Q4 FY26).

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for expansion into six new divisions, including pharma and specialty chemicals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it an enabling board resolution covering multiple options (including EV and an advanced technology centre). Nothing is decided yet. Significant decisions will be disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: How secure is the TMD order book and what is the domestic visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: The ₹3,200 cr is secured through 10% deposits. Demand is recovering gradually, with state policies and FTAs as triggers. Cotton spinning margins are good, while synthetics are under strain.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the order book by customer type and project versus unitary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose customer-level detail. The order mix is about 70% projects and 30% unitary machines, against 60:40 in good years.

qa_highlights.question: ATC capacity expansion, margin outlook, and whether forex helped?
qa_highlights.answer: A ~₹150 cr land and building plan is due over 18-24 months. Q1 margin was higher on mix (more assemblies). Forex was a positive, with the ATC margin range at 94-96% after a jump from 85 to 95 last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of USD and EUR appreciation on MTD costs and mitigation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the currency impact is real on MTD and textile costs. Mitigation includes India-sourced parts and price revisions, and ATC and foundry have contractual price-revision clauses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses grow only ~4% YoY while revenue grew ~25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited ongoing cost optimisation and a VRS cost booked in the last quarter, with a tight cost belt maintained as ATC, MTD and textile pick up.

qa_highlights.question: Path back to 12-14% MTD EBIT margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Requires turnover growth and higher utilisation on a much larger cost base; no timeline was given.

risks_watch: Margin recovery: MTD operating margin fell on lower turnover; management gave no timeline for returning to the 12-14% EBIT range it cited, and said it depends on turnover growth and utilisation.

Currency and input costs: management confirmed USD/EUR impact on MTD and textile costs, with raw material and logistics costs up about 3-3.5%; mitigation depends on India-sourced parts and price revisions, with pass-through not quantified.
Order book conversion: TMD order book of ₹3,200 cr with ~₹2,400 cr active; management did not give a timeline for conversion or the customer-level split.
ATC execution: ~₹900-1,000 cr export order book over 3-3.5 years needs ~₹150 cr land and building capex over 18-24 months; composite share (~20% of turnover, ~25% of order book) remains low.
Textile utilisation: management gave ~60% in a later answer versus 75-80% for MTD, so the utilisation figure needs clarification.
Other expenses rose only ~4% YoY against revenue growth of ~25%, which management attributed partly to a VRS cost booked in the last quarter; sustainability of this cost base is unclear.

summary.management_tone: Confident on the order book, ATC export visibility and the state-policy demand outlook, but cautious on MTD margins, which management did not give a timeline for recovering. Evasive on customer-level order detail, the textile competitor question and the Q1 textile utilisation figure, which was given inconsistently (75-80% for MTD, ~60% for textile).
